responsibility: This module is the GCC target backend for the Vitesse IQ2000 architecture, responsible for turning generic GCC RTL and target hooks into IQ2000-specific code generation, ABI behavior, and assembly output. Its central implementation files provide the procedural target logic for calling conventions, varargs and return values, frame layout and prologue/epilogue expansion, address legitimization, cost and legality decisions, builtin support, delay-slot handling, and final operand or instruction printing, while the target header defines the machine model seen by the rest of GCC, including data layout, register classes, stack conventions, and register-allocation rules. The machine-description files supply the declarative instruction selector and scheduler view of the processor through RTL patterns, attributes, delay-slot rules, predicates, and operand constraints, and the option files define IQ2000-specific -march/-mcpu and feature selection interfaces. Together, these pieces make this module the architecture-specific RTL expansion, instruction selection, scheduling, and emission layer for IQ2000, distinguishing it from generic middle-end code and from other target ports by encoding the IQ2000 ISA, ABI, and tuning behavior.
